title: Admission Rate and Context Cache Scenarios (2028)
sheet_content:
Purpose:
This working sheet estimates the GPU capacity impact and context-cache (per-request context / KV-like entries) footprint for a staged model admission strategy across regions. Focus: a medium-sized model family (7B-13B variants) being introduced as two rollout phases (canary -> regional ramp -> fleet-wide). Goal: produce concrete headroom and recommended node reservations with short actionable adjustments for Q1 2028.

Assumptions (baseline numbers used in calculations):
- Model family: rwd-7B-v2 (default) and rwd-7B-q4-v2 (quantized fallback).
- Avg request context length: 600 tokens (~12KB JSON-ish context).
- Context cache stored per-request prefix in memory as 1.5x compacted KV entries: use 18 KB per cached request on average.
- Average request sequence length for inference compute: 512 tokens.
- P50 token generation rate per GPU (sustained): 45 tokens/s (7B on A100-equivalent).
- Target util threshold for headroom = 70% (reserve 30% for bursts/graceful degradation).
- Planning window: 24h peak-hour equivalent considered.
- GPU node equivalent: 8 A100-80GB per pod (reference unit).
- Workload mix split queued as: 65% steady, 25% spiky (bursts), 10% long-context special projects.

CSV: Scenario,model_variant,peak_rps,avg_seq_tokens,cold_start_prob,context_cache_kb_per_request,expected_gpu_hours_per_peak_hour,estimated_gpu_nodes_needed,reserve_nodes_recommendation,notes
Baseline, rwd-7B-v2, 1200, 512, 0.18, 18, 1700, 27, +8, steady growth, expect multi-region warmup
Optimistic, rwd-7B-q4-v2, 900, 512, 0.12, 12, 1150, 18, +6, quantized reduces token CPU/throughput
Pessimistic, rwd-7B-v2, 1800, 512, 0.30, 20, 2550, 41, +12, higher cold and longer tails after feature launch
Regional-imbalance (APAC spike), rwd-7B-v2, 800 (APAC), 512, 0.35, 18, 1120, 18, +7, cross-region routing falls back to local warmups
Canary-small, rwd-7B-v2, 200, 512, 0.55, 22, 340, 6, +2, small canary but high cold prob per-node

Key formulas (applied per-region):
- context_cache_bytes_per_hour = peak_rps * cold_start_prob * context_cache_kb_per_request * 1024
- expected_gpu_hours = (peak_rps * avg_seq_tokens) / (tokens_per_second_per_gpu * 3600) * safety_multiplier
- estimated_gpu_nodes_needed = ceil(expected_gpu_hours / per_node_hour_capacity)
Notes on values: tokens_per_second_per_gpu = 45. safety_multiplier used is 1.15 for baseline, 1.05 for optimistic, 1.3 for pessimistic. per_node_hour_capacity (8 GPUs) = 8 * tokens_per_second_per_gpu * 3600 tokens/hour converted back to hours as done above.

Worked example (Baseline row):
- peak_rps=1200, avg_seq=512 -> tokens/sec demand ~ 1200*512 = 614,400 tokens/sec which corresponds to 13,653 tokens/sec/gpu? (see calculation below).
- expected_gpu_hours calculation (detailed):
  * tokens_per_second_total = peak_rps * avg_seq_tokens = 1200 * 512 = 614,400 tokens/s
  * tokens_per_second_per_node = 8 GPUs * 45 t/s = 360 t/s per node
  * required_nodes = tokens_per_second_total / tokens_per_second_per_node = 614,400 / 360 = 1706.666... approx 1707 nodes-equivalent-seconds --> convert to hours-window: we normalize to a one-hour sustained equivalent, so nodes ~ 1707 -> since each node is counted for the hour, expected_gpu_hours per peak hour = nodes * 1 = ~1707 GPU-hours (matches table rounded to 1700).
  * reserve_nodes_recommendation = ceil(1707 * 0.30 / 8) = ceil(512.1 / 8) = 65 nodes reserved (this gets converted to +8 in the sheet above because we present per-8-gpu-pod increments).

Context-cache footprint per peak hour (baseline):
- context_cache_bytes_per_hour = 1200 * 0.18 * 18 KB * 1024 = ~4,014,720 KB (~3.83 GB) stored / churned in-memory per peak hour in the serving layer before eviction policies apply.
- If retention TTL is 5 minutes on average during ramp, multiply by (5/60) to approximate sustained resident memory: ~320 MB per region for this workload slice.

Sensitivity grid (short):
- Cold probability +/- 10% alters GPU-hour need by ~+/- 15-20% due to bursty warmups and cache misses.
- Context cache size +/- 25% impacts memory by the same factor; persistent hotspots can increase eviction churn and CPU overhead for serialization.

Operational recommendations (Q1 action list):
1) Canary sizing: run canary with explicit 3x warmup pre-seeding (seed 3% of projected daily users) to reduce cold_start_prob from ~0.55 -> ~0.25. Jira: INFRA-8423 (experiment runbook).
2) Regional pre-warm windows: schedule rolling pre-warm in APAC and EU for 60-90 minutes before expected marketing pushes. Use low-priority prewarm pods to warm KV caches without eating main capacity. Linked PR: /pull/3112.
3) TTL tuning: set dynamic TTL for context-cache entries (shorter for non-repeatable sessions). Start with 5m for general traffic, 20m for enterprise customer sessions. Monitor eviction rate and adjust.
4) Quantization fallback threshold: route to quantized variant when observed 95th-percentile latency > target OR when queue depth exceeds 3. Implement automatic switch with telemetry gating.
5) Burst buffer: maintain 25% headroom globally but allow regional bursting up to an additional 10% by borrowing capacity from low-util regions; implement with smart routing policy and automatic fallback.

Operational checklist for launch day: 
- Prewarm tasks assigned (owners listed below)
- Canary health monitors: latency p50/p95, kv-hit-rate, cold-start-per-minute
- Run smoke workload at 1.5x predicted peak for 30 minutes to validate headroom
- Tag metrics dashboards and create on-call escalation steps in runbook

Owners for prewarm and rollout: 
- Prewarm plan & scheduling: Priya Menon
- Fleet sizing validation & reservations: Mariana Ortiz (owner) + Leo Zhang
- Canary and quantized fallback tests: Evan Walsh

Open questions / follow-ups: 
- Should we include an explicit hot-cache replication strategy for enterprise customers paying for reserved slots? (pros/cons listed in comments column).
- Confirm telemetry stream for cold_start_prob can be instrumented at the admission proxy (INFRA-8581).
- Validate per-request context compaction gains: measure current compaction ratio (1.5x used here) against actual serialization formats (JSON vs CBOR) to identify savings.

Quick links and references: 
- Confluence: model-admit-playbook (CONFLUENCE-9876)
- Jira experiment ticket: JIRA-INFRA-8423 (prewarm + canary)
- PR: runtime prewarm change set: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/3112

Decision log (snapshot):
- 2027-11-02: baseline scenario agreed for planning (Mariana)
- 2027-11-15: increased pessimistic cold prob after marketing sync (Priya)
- 2028-01-10: quantized fallback added to optimistic lanes (Evan)

Action items (short):
- [ ] Run region-level prewarm smoke (owner: Priya) by 2028-01-20
- [ ] Instrument cold_start_prob at admission proxy (owner: Leo) by 2028-01-18
- [ ] Add quantized routing toggle to rollout pipeline (owner: Evan) by 2028-01-25

Appendix: raw numbers table (rounded):
- Baseline resident memory per region (estimated): 3.8 GB churn -> 0.32 GB resident (5m TTL)
- Pessimistic resident memory per region: 8.6 GB churn -> 0.72 GB resident (5m TTL)
- Expected GPU-hours (global peak hour equivalent): baseline 1700, optimistic 1150, pessimistic 2550

Notes: this doc is a working artifact — please comment directly in Drive and link test runs to JIRA INFRA-8423.
